content: Researching the reported timeline-order/tool-content issue against current shared/host/mobile code, Pi session export source, TUI spinner behavior, and pi-mono web UI components before implementation.

observation: Current mobile UI shows thinking text as one long block before several tool cards, and tool cards only show the tool title/status (`Tool done`) without arguments or returned text output.
TUI reference shows tool execution blocks as expanded green cards containing the invoked command and output, not just a status line.

Pi web UI renders assistant `message.content` in a single ordered loop: text chunks become `markdown-block`, thinking chunks become `thinking-block`, and toolCall chunks become `tool-message` paired with matching tool results. This is the desired ordering model for mobile.

The HTML export currently renders assistant text/thinking in one loop and tool calls in a second loop, which is less useful for preserving interleaving; however its `renderToolCall()` implementation is useful for expanded tool call/result display (bash command, read/write/edit/ls args, result text/images, custom fallbacks).

The TUI working indicator uses `Loader` with Braille frames `⠋ ⠙ ⠹ ⠸ ⠼ ⠴ ⠦ ⠧ ⠇ ⠏`, 80ms interval, accent-colored spinner, muted `Working...` text. React Native can reproduce this with `useEffect`/`setInterval` state while `runState` is streaming or compacting.

Pi web UI default tool rendering always shows input JSON and output text when available; BashRenderer combines `> command` plus output in a console block. Mobile should store tool args and text output in `ToolItem` and render both fully expanded for now.

Pi web UI's `markdown-block` comes from mini-lit/web components and the HTML export embeds marked/highlight.js; neither is directly reusable in React Native. A native dependency such as `react-native-markdown-display` is the practical mobile equivalent for rendering user/assistant markdown.

Mobile currently tracks only one active assistant item and one active thinking item, so later assistant/thinking deltas in the same run can append to earlier blocks and appear before intervening tool cards. Host snapshot application also appends every `timeline_item` instead of upserting, which can duplicate tool start/end updates in snapshots.

title: Research local browser rendering mismatch and identify why real read tools show `read ...`
Preserve tool call arguments across tool updates/end events and update tests
Validate argument preservation fix and push PR update

content: Investigating the user's local browser screenshot mismatch. The screenshot shows the new read renderer is active, but the read tool has no args by the time it renders (`read ...`) and therefore no language for syntax highlighting.

observation: The user's local browser screenshot is using the new ReadToolCard path (title renders `read ...`), but the item has no preserved args: no Arguments section appears, the path falls back to `...`, and read output is plain gray because getReadLanguage() cannot infer a language without args.path/file_path.

Pi agent events include args on `tool_execution_start` and `tool_execution_update`, but `tool_execution_end` only carries toolCallId/toolName/result/isError. The mobile timeline currently replaces the existing tool item on every upsert, so the final end item drops the start args.

projectPiEvent() creates a new ToolItem for start/update/end. For `tool_execution_end`, the created item omits args when event.args is undefined, which explains real read cards becoming `read ...` after completion. The previous mock smoke did not catch this because its final read item included args.

Both mobile reducer and host runner upsert timeline items by replacing the entire item with the same ID. Fixing projection to emit end items with preserved args will repair both live rendering and host snapshots.

content: Root cause identified: real Pi `tool_execution_end` events do not include args, and the current timeline projection replaces the started tool item with an end item that has no args. This causes `read ...` and disables read language detection/highlighting.
Implementing argument preservation in the shared timeline projection so update/end tool items retain the started tool title, createdAt, args, and prior detail when event fields are omitted.

Implemented the fix in `packages/shared/src/timeline.ts` by adding `activeToolItems` to `TimelineProjectionState`. Tool projection now preserves the first tool item's title, createdAt, args, and prior detail when later update/end events omit fields. Added a regression test proving a `read` start with path/offset/limit followed by a `tool_execution_end` without args still emits the final done item with the original args and start timestamp.

Argument preservation implementation is complete. Proceeding to full validation and PR update.
Running full validation for the argument preservation fix, then will commit and push the PR update.
